title: The fixed Koszul tower computes integral reduction on any representative
statement: Fix prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, a scheme Y and finite-field datum D with l different from its characteristic. Use the completed integral module and derived categories of [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models]. Let q:P to G be a K-flat resolution and N any complex with an isomorphism Q(N) to Q(G). For R the completed coefficient sheaf and a its constant uniformizer, let Q_n=[R --a^(n+1)--> R] with strict transitions (a,id), as in [def-pur-principal-koszul-quotient-towers]. Then the actual integralReductionTower(P) of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] is isomorphic to the functor n maps to localization of totalTensor(N,Q_n), with its tensor-induced transitions. No Hom functor or representative of a Hom object occurs in this assertion.

proof.text: Apply the existing coefficient augmentation quasi-isomorphism from the principal strict replacement to the given K-flat P. K-flat tensor invariance applies with P in the second variable; the signed cochain braiding conjugates it to id_P tensor epsilon_n. Thus the existing strict augmentation comparison is objectwise a quasi-isomorphism without any flat-term hypothesis on P. Tensor-colimit preservation supplies the cochain braiding instances.

Use the proved scalarTowerIso underlying finite_reduction_scalar_normalization, which is defined for every complex, to identify the strict restricted-quotient tensor tower with the ordinary scalar-reduction tower. The existing integralTowerTransition_eq identifies its consecutive transitions with the actual integralReductionTower transitions. Localize this tower isomorphism and invert the localized augmentation comparison.

The existing koszul_flat and koszul_bounded lemmas show that every coefficient Koszul complex is bounded above with flat terms. Apply the independent-universe bounded-flat theorem to obtain K-flatness. Form the functor sending N to the localized tower of N tensor Q_n; K-flat tensor invariance makes it invert all quasi-isomorphisms, objectwise and hence as tower morphisms.

Apply the universal property of DerivedCategory.Q via Localization.lift and Localization.fac to descend the entire tower functor. Its comparison isomorphisms transport the composite Q(P) to Q(G) to Q(N), obtained from the quasi-isomorphism q and the inverse of e. Compose this transported tower isomorphism with step 2. All constructions retain every tower arrow; n=0 is exponent one, and neither boundedness nor flatness of N is assumed.

theorem integralReductionTower_koszul_model
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}) (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{d}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (P G N : CochainComplex (completedIntegralModuleSheaves l E Y D hl) ℤ)
    (q : P ⟶ G)
    (hq : CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolutionIndependentCoefficients
      (J := AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
      (R := completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E Y D hl) q)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj N ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G) :
    Nonempty (integralReductionTower l E Y D hl P ≅
      principalKoszulTower (completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E Y D hl)
        (PrincipalKoszulStrictReplacement.uniformizer l E Y) ⋙
          (totalTensor.{t, u} Y (completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E Y D hl)).obj N ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Q)
